name: pre-read-after-own-stop-and-a-peer-commit-denies-with-the-write-wording
description: The read a session keeps when its turn ends is still made stale by a peer (#513). Session A reads notes.md (v1), pre-edits it, commits v2 and its turn ends, so it is a reader of v2. Peer B then pre-edits notes.md and commits v3, which makes A's copy INVALID. A's next Read is denied with the write wording naming B (agent 814dac78), exactly as a reader that never edited the file is denied in row 01. The summary is asserted too: prior_version_seen_by_session must be 2, the version A held when it let go, current_version must be 3, B's commit, and last_writer_session_id must be B's agent id, which both backends derive the same way (its 32-char hex form is compared as written). A offers the hash of the v2 bytes it holds and B's commit carries other bytes, so hash_differs is true. Both backends.

hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason: Stale read denied: notes.md was updated by agent 814dac78 at <TS>. Re-read notes.md via the Read tool before proceeding. This denial is structural (v0.2 strict mode); retrying the same operation will produce the same denial.
